headline: Google says its internal AI agent PageBreak has found and proven more than 500 web security flaws in Google's own applications.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a company claim of notable scale, not independently verified, disclosure date unclear.
importance_line: Google's security engineers get fewer false alarms and users of its services get faster fixes, but the figures are Google's own and have not been independently checked.
summary: GBHackers reports that Google has disclosed an internal AI security agent called PageBreak, which found and confirmed more than 500 cross-site scripting flaws, a type of bug that lets an attacker run their own code in a web page, across Google's own web applications. Google says the agent reports only flaws it can prove by reproducing the exploit, which gives a near-zero false-positive rate, and it is a company claim not yet independently checked.
notes: Google's original disclosure not read; the date of the disclosure is not stated in the article, so freshness NEW is an assumption.
